findings.desc: p.165 page marker placed two lines late: the PDF page turn is after 'This is not because' (last line of p.164), but the md puts <!-- p.165 --> after '…but the monitor flagged every one.', so p.165's first two lines ('the models fail at the side task—Claude Mythos 5.2, … flagged every one.') are attributed to p.164 and the served p.165 gutter label sits mid-paragraph at the wrong spot. Same root as the p.165 paragraph merge (reported there as major).
findings.evidence: p-164.png last line ends 'This is not because'; p-165.png opens 'the models fail at the side task—'; sections/06c-alignment-3.md line 81 '…flagged every one.<!-- p.165 --> However, …'; served.html id="p-165" anchor follows 'flagged every one.'; glyph count check: p.164 slice has one extra ’ and — that the PDF prints on p.165

findings.desc:
Two PDF paragraphs merged into one: 'None of the models can kill … but the monitor flagged every one.' (p.164→p.165, ends on p.165 line 2) and the next paragraph 'However, when the monitor couldn’t see the model’s reasoning … harder for the monitor to detect.' are separated by a blank-line paragraph gap in the PDF, but the md/HTML joins them into a single

with the p.165 page anchor between them. Likely cause: PyMuPDF returns all of p.165's body as ONE block (bbox 72,72–543,523), and the seam stitcher appended the whole first paragraph of p.165 plus the next one as the continuation.
findings.evidence:
p-165.png: clear paragraph gap between 'flagged every one.' and 'However, when'; sections/06c-alignment-3.md line 81 single paragraph '…flagged every one. However, when the monitor…'; served.html one

containing both; pymupdf dict p.165 shows a single text block for the whole page body
